messages:
mira: Quick follow-up on yesterday's allocator cleanup RFC — went through a small spike repro and had a couple of questions about the proposed split between allocation and residency APIs.

mira: Summary: we want alloc() to be deterministic and cheap, and push placement/residency decisions to a new residency_manager that can batch/delay offload decisions.

tariq: SGTM in principle. main worry is the latency tail for small requests if residency_manager adds async hops. did you measure p99 impact?

mira: I ran a microbench: baseline (current monolith) p50=1.2ms p99=12.4ms; with residency_manager local-pathing (fast-path for hot slices) p50=1.3ms p99=13.1ms; with async offload hinting enabled p99 jumps to ~25ms in our small-batch fixture.

jon: 25ms is rough but acceptable if we can bound it and provide SLO knobs. Could we add a synchronous hot-path: alloc+ensure_resident(token) for callers needing bounded latency?

mira: That's exactly the compromise I sketched. API idea: alloc(size, flags) -> handle; ensure_resident(handle, policy="sync|hint|defer") -> future/ok. Default hint keeps alloc cheap.

evan: Two interface boundary questions: 1) who owns eviction decisions (tenant vs platform), 2) how do we surface memory pressure signals so residency_manager doesn't thrash?

tariq: For (1) platform should own global heuristics but tenants can provide soft hints (e.g. affinity, lifetime). For (2) we already emit watermarks from host-pool; maybe residency_manager subscribes and uses backpressure tokens.

mira: Implementation concern: we currently piggyback eviction metadata on the allocation descriptors. If we split, we need an idempotent mapping and GC strategy for dangling residency entries. Also need fast-path for handle -> gpu_ptr for kernels.

jon: Maybe keep a compact handle that is either direct pointer (if resident) or an indirection slot index. indirection table lives in shm and residency_manager updates it atomically. That keeps the kernel path cheap.

mira: Good. Also thinking about fragmentation: when residency_manager delays placement, we risk scattering small live ranges across the host/gpu. We should add a compaction hint API: compact_candidates(range_id, urgency).

evan: Compaction needs to be bounded cost. Proposal: make compaction cooperative: kernels mark long-lived pinned ranges -> residency_manager treats those as compaction anchors. Then background compactor migrates ephemeral stuff around them.

mira: Open question: how to expose quantization/packing decisions to residency logic. e.g., 4-bit packed tensors want co-located pages. Maybe a "packing_group" tag on alloc handles so residency_manager can colocate/stripe.

tariq: ++ packing_group sounds neat. We should test impact on eviction locality and KV cache efficiency.

mira: Action items: 1) I'll prototype handle indirection + ensure_resident sync path (PR in next sprint). 2) jon to spec residency_manager watermark integration with host-pool. 3) evan to draft compaction anchor semantics and packing_group tag.

infra-bot: deploybot: CI pipeline queued for mira/allocator-prototype branch.

mira: Also, we should add a quick in-prod metric: "residency_ensure_latency" tagged by policy (sync|hint|defer) and outcome (hit|miss|evict_fallback). Will help validate SLO knobs.

jon: If no objections I'll add the API sketch to the RFC doc and we can iterate.

tariq: no objections from me. thanks for the writeup mira. :thumbsup:

mira: thanks everyone — will post the PR and a short benchmark with small-batch p99 before/after.
